title: IBM Research Automates QEC Decoder Chip Design Using Open AI Agent Factories at 11.5x Lower Inference Cost - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM Research used AI agent factories to automate high-level-synthesis design of QEC decoder hardware for the Relay-BP decoder on the Gross qLDPC code, reaching up to 204x speedup with proprietary models and 52x for $26 using open-weight models, an 11.5x inference cost saving.

insights.claim: IBM's agent factory achieved up to a 204x hardware speedup (139 microseconds) on Relay-BP decoder HLS designs using an all-proprietary Claude Opus 5 configuration, costing $299.45 and 215.9M tokens.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Frontier models deliver the best speedup but at the highest inference cost.

insights.claim: An all-open-weight configuration (GLM-5.3 with llm-d) gave a 52x speedup for about $25.95, 11.5x cheaper than the proprietary baseline, while a hybrid Opus-coordinator/GLM-worker setup gave 126x at $105.25 (2.8x cheaper).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Open-weight models offer a cost-performance tradeoff that makes autonomous chip design practical.

insights.claim: Extending the all-open run to a 200-hypothesis budget raised speedup only to 60x at roughly double the cost (~$52), which the table labels diminishing returns.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: More search budget on open models yields limited incremental gain.

insights.claim: Serving open-weight models on-premises with the open-source llm-d stack gave a 98% prefix-cache hit rate and reduced blended serving cost to about $0.11 per million tokens.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Efficient self-hosted inference is the lever that cuts AI-agent compute costs.

insights.claim: qLDPC codes reduce physical-to-logical qubit overhead versus 2D surface codes, but their dense non-local check matrices demand complex parallel classical decoding hardware, which the agent factory targets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Classical decoder hardware is a bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum systems.

insights.claim: The framework pairs a coordinator model with four parallel worker agents proposing architectural transformations such as check-major memory layouts, unrolled loop reductions and dual-layout message stores to reach Initiation Interval II = 1.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows a replicable multi-agent pattern for hardware design space exploration.
